candidate_extension.name: Ordered containment fallback lookup
exact_rule_text: `p ?= e1 ?= e2` is one ordered fallback chain. Evaluate p's authored occurrence first. Only when p has occurrence `{=0}` evaluate e1; only when e1 is absent evaluate e2. An authored occurrence of p, including an invalid one, is never skipped.

`LOOKUP(R, q)` starts at p's selected bearer and follows one-or-more existing R links away from that bearer. It returns the value of the nearest bearer that has an authored occurrence of compatible logical Property q. Nearer matches take precedence over farther matches.

`LOOKUP(R, T{:1}, q)` follows that same ordered R chain to exactly one terminal selected by T, then returns q on that terminal bearer. The `{:1}` terminal binding is part of this expression: zero or more-than-one matching terminal is an error.

Each traversed bearer is inspected only for q resolved by full Property declaration identity in the selected effective MODEL. Equal bare names from another declaration do not match. If q is not applicable to a bearer, no q slot, Property, or value is invented there.

Absence of an applicable authored q occurrence permits the next lookup step. A present q that violates its declaration, has missing or multiple required values, or is otherwise unresolved is invalid and errors; it is not skipped. An unresolved or multiple R target at any traversed step, a cycle, an unresolved terminal, or incompatible fallback value errors.

The fallback remains non-writing: it resolves an effective value without copying a value to p, changing p's authored occurrence, creating a Property, or creating an R link. It cannot satisfy a required authored occurrence.
Lookup is lazy. An unevaluated later branch need not resolve; once an earlier authored or valid fallback value is selected, later branches—including a malformed chain—are not evaluated.
candidate_extension.scope_boundary: This is one reusable relation-chain lookup shape, not a general path, ancestry, projection, or inherited-instance-value language. It follows only the named R chain in the expression.

examples.name: plan-authored-value-short-circuits
examples.state: Plan has authored valid value 80; containment chain is cyclic or unavailable.
examples.result: effective 80; LOOKUP branches are not evaluated.

examples.name: nearest-compatible-ancestor-wins
examples.state: Plan omits the Property; nearest chain bearer has an authored valid occurrence resolved to the same Plan-property declaration identity with value 75; terminal required Project Settings value is 60.
examples.result: effective 75; terminal branch is not evaluated.

examples.name: inapplicable-scope-unit-does-not-create-slot
examples.state: Plan omits the Property; an intervening Scope Unit has no applicable matching declaration; same-chain Project terminal has required value 60.
examples.result: effective 60; no Scope Unit Property is inferred.

examples.name: same-bare-name-is-not-a-match
examples.state: Plan omits the Property; an ancestor bears a different declaration also named AI Agent Confidence Threshold with value 70; Project terminal has 60.
examples.result: effective 60; the different declaration identity is ignored.

examples.name: invalid-nearest-source-errors
examples.state: Plan omits the Property; nearest compatible authored source has two values or a non-int value; Project terminal has 60.
examples.result: error; invalid source is not skipped to the terminal.

examples.name: missing-required-terminal-errors
examples.state: Plan and all compatible ancestors omit the Property; same-chain Project Settings leaf is absent.
examples.result: error; the required terminal contract has been violated and no value is fabricated.

examples.name: multiple-parent-step-errors
examples.state: Plan omits the Property and one traversed bearer has two IS_CONTAINED_BY targets.
examples.result: error; lookup never chooses an arbitrary path.

examples.name: multiple-project-terminals-error
examples.state: Plan omits the Property and its chain resolves two Project terminals.
